column2: THE HAND: drawn with a crow-quill dip pen in black ink: fine springy lines that swell and taper with pressure, tiny ink blots where the nib paused, cross-hatching only in the few darkest spots. THE SUBJECT: a small cartoonish island in a calm sea: a ring of sandy beach, four or five palm trees, a crooked little lighthouse with a striped tower standing on a rocky point, a short wooden jetty with one small sailboat. The sea around the island is shown only by sparse little wave strokes that reach out toward the edges of the square.

THE HAND: painted with a Chinese ink brush in black ink: bold, wet, calligraphic strokes with strong thick-to-thin variation and dry-brush edges, very economical, perhaps forty strokes in total. THE SUBJECT: an open grassland steppe: three round felt yurts with thin smoke wisps, four small horses grazing, a winding stream, and one big jagged rocky mountain peak rising at the back of the plot.

THE HAND: drawn with a 0.3 mm technical pen in black ink: uniform-width lines, every tone built from careful parallel hatching and cross-hatching, like a naturalist's or architect's pen drawing. THE SUBJECT: a dense forest of tall pointed pine trees covering most of the plot, with one small clearing holding a log cabin with a smoking chimney, a small round pond and a footpath winding to it.

THE HAND: drawn with a soft graphite pencil, grey graphite on white: loose sketchy lines, a few construction lines left in, light side-of-the-pencil shading on the shadow side of each dune, a smudge or two. THE SUBJECT: a desert of big rolling sand dunes with long curving ridges, one tall lattice-steel radio signal tower with a small hut at its foot, a few rocks and a faint line of camel footprints.

THE HAND: drawn with a black wax crayon / grease pencil: chunky, waxy, grainy lines with the paper tooth showing through, confident and loose, no fine detail. THE SUBJECT: a tight stacked city of tall narrow towers with curved Chinese tiled roofs, many hanging vertical shop signs and strings of lanterns between buildings, a big gate arch at the front, small bridges between towers.

THE HAND: drawn with a cheap ballpoint pen in black: thin lines, scribbled back-and-forth shading, a few repeated nervous lines. THE SUBJECT: a farm valley of patchwork fields with crop rows, one windmill, a barn, a fence line and a lone tree.

THE HAND: drawn with a thick black felt-tip marker: blunt rounded lines, all the same weight, slight bleed where the marker paused. THE SUBJECT: a small castle with three towers on a round hill, a road spiralling up the hill, a few round bushes at the bottom.

THE HAND: drawn with a fine black fineliner in stippling: outlines plus tones made only of dots, denser in the shadows. THE SUBJECT: a cone volcano with a crater and a thin smoke plume, lava channels running down one side, a few boulders and a tiny hut at its foot.

THE HAND: drawn with a stick of black charcoal: soft broad smeary lines, rough grainy edges, bold dark accents. THE SUBJECT: a red-rock canyon country: two flat-topped mesas, a deep winding canyon between them crossed by a small rope bridge, a few cacti.

THE HAND: painted ONLY with a big soft Chinese calligraphy brush and black sumi ink, like a quick sumi-e painting: NO pen lines at all, no fine outlines, no hatching. Every mark is a brush stroke: wet, bold, thick-to-thin, with ragged dry-brush streaks where the brush ran out of ink; the mountain is a few big sweeping strokes with dry-brush texture, the grass is quick flicks. Very economical: about forty strokes in total, lots of white paper. THE SUBJECT: an open grassland steppe: three round felt yurts (each a dome and a door, a thin smoke wisp), three small horses as quick brush gestures, a winding stream as one ribbon of strokes, and one big jagged mountain peak at the back.

THE HAND: drawn ONLY with a blunt black wax crayon on rough paper, like a child-friendly but skilled crayon sketch: thick grainy waxy lines about 6 px wide with broken speckled edges where the paper tooth shows, wobbly hand-drawn verticals, no fine lines, no hatching with a pen, no tiny details, rough crayon scribble fill on the roofs. THE SUBJECT: a tight cluster of five tall narrow tower buildings stacked together with curved Chinese tiled roofs, big hanging vertical shop signs (blank rectangles) and strings of round lanterns between the towers, a big gate arch at the front.

THE HAND: a quick loose urban-sketcher drawing with a fountain pen: fast gestural lines, unfinished edges, scribbled windows, lines that don't quite meet. THE SUBJECT: a small harbour town on a curved bay: a cluster of houses with pitched roofs, a stone quay, three small boats, a short breakwater with a light at its end.

THE HAND: drawn with a blue-black ballpoint, but render it in black: scribbly loops and zig-zag shading, the pen never lifts for long. THE SUBJECT: snowy mountain peaks with a glacier tongue flowing down between them, a small wooden hut with a flag, a frozen lake.

THE HAND: drawn with a fine dip pen in quick confident outlines with no shading at all, a few loose ink splatters. THE SUBJECT: old stone ruins in a jungle: a stepped stone pyramid temple, broken columns, big round-leaved jungle trees and hanging vines.

THE HAND: drawn with a brush pen (felt brush tip): springy lines with a clear thick-thin swell, quick and rhythmic. THE SUBJECT: curving rice terraces stepping down a hillside, a small pagoda-roofed farmhouse, a few people-free paths between terraces, a stream.

THE HAND: drawn with a soft 6B pencil, grey graphite: loose, quick, smudged tone, a few construction lines left in. THE SUBJECT: a ring of old standing stones on a grassy rise, a single crooked tree, a sheep path winding past, low drystone walls.

THE HAND: drawn with a fine dip pen with sepia-like black ink in a loose, sketchy, slightly naive way: lines that wander, uneven hatching. THE SUBJECT: a fishing village of wooden huts on stilts over a shallow lagoon, plank walkways between them, two canoes, fishing nets hung to dry.

THE HAND: drawn with a 0.5 mm technical pen, clean even lines, stippled shading only. THE SUBJECT: a domed observatory on a rocky hilltop, a switchback road climbing to it, a few boulders and dry shrubs.

THE HAND: drawn with a thick black felt-tip marker, bold and cartoonish, every line the same weight. THE SUBJECT: a small fairground: a ferris wheel, a striped tent, a carousel, a few lamp posts and bunting strings.

THE HAND: painted with a Chinese ink brush in black ink, quick sumi-e strokes, wet and dry brush, very economical. THE SUBJECT: a bamboo grove on a slope, a little tea house with a curved roof, a stone path and a small waterfall.

THE HAND: drawn with a black wax crayon: grainy, chunky, broken waxy lines, scribbled fill, no fine detail. THE SUBJECT: a desert oasis: a round pond, a cluster of date palms, two tents, a camel lying down, a few rocks.

THE HAND: drawn with a black ballpoint pen: thin nervous lines, scribbled cross-hatching, the pen barely lifts. THE SUBJECT: a stepped stone quarry cut into a hill, a little crane, a cart track, stacked stone blocks and a small hut.

THE HAND: drawn with a stick of black charcoal: soft broad smeary lines, grainy edges, bold dark accents. THE SUBJECT: a misty swamp: twisted mangrove trees with roots, a boardwalk zig-zagging across the water, a small shack on piles, lily pads.
